newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Margins to pinch Mobil, majors.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Margins to pinch Mobil, majors.

text.p: A fire that trimmed output from a key Mobil Corp refinery last month was expected to dampen third quarter earnings for the oil company, analysts said.

Analysts have been cutting earnings estimates for the Fairfax, Va.-based major since the fire, driving the consensus to $1.69 a share for the quarter compared to $1.95 a share earnings reported in the same period last year.
"(The refinery) was down at a time when margins on the West Coast were quite strong. They were forced to be a buyer instead of a seller," Schroder Wertheim's Michael Mayer said.
As the majors prepare to release third quarter earnings on Monday, analysts said the quarter will hinge on whether the recent surge in crude prices offset weak refining margins.

"The real key is the degree of the profitability on the exploration and production side. Refining and marketing has not been good, so they'll have to make it up on the other side," Robert W. Baird & Co analyst George Gaspar said.
"Domestic refining and marketing is going to be a source of weakness for third quarter earnings," Salomon Brothers energy analyst Paul Ting said in a recent report.
Ting characterized California refining margins as "strong," Gulf Coast margins "in the red," and East Coast margins "anemic."

Still, analysts in recent weeks have been steadily raising estimates on most domestic oil majors on the ongoing rally in crude prices upstream, which have driven front-month crude above $25 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Upside surprises could be posted by Phillips Petroleum Co from strong crude and natural gas production, and by Amerada Hess Corp, which has benefited from strong distillate prices, analysts said.
In the wake of Mobil's September 6 fire at the Torrance, Calif., refinery in the Los Angeles suburbs, most analysts tracking the company cut estimates for third quarter earnings.
The early morning fire at the 130,000 barrel per day refinery cut output of high-octane gasoline at a time when prices were surging higher in West Coast cash markets.
A Mobil spokesman said the fire's impact probably was not severe enough to have a material impact on third quarter results, and the company met its committments to customers.
"I would be surprised if it's a very big chunk (out of earnings)," the spokesman said.
